title: Why Chile is so long and thin

hooks.text: This country is 24 times longer than it is wide.
Why is Chile shaped like that?
Chile is longer than Europe is tall.
One treaty turned a mountain range into a country's shape.
This is Chile. It should not look like this.
You could cross this country in a morning. Top to bottom takes days.

hookVariants.visual: Frame 0 tight on Chile's narrow middle, the teal width bar across it, '24X LONGER THAN IT IS WIDE' beside it; the camera snaps back (12 f) to the whole country as the gold ruler drops from the northern tip; 24 width tiles stack along it.
Frame 0 shows all of South America with Chile already red; the camera snaps in to the whole country as the ruler drops from the northern tip; '24X' beside it; 24 tiles stack.
Frame 0 is the whole country already measured (gold ruler down its length, '24X' beside it); a short push, the teal width bar snaps across the middle, 24 tiles stack.

beats.text: This country is 24 times longer than it is *wide.*
beats.visual: Tight on Chile's narrow red middle with a teal width bar across it and '24X LONGER THAN IT IS WIDE'; snap back to the whole country as a gold ruler drops down its length; 24 teal width tiles stack beside the ruler.

beats.text: Chile runs *4,270* kilometers from top to bottom.
beats.visual: Flat map, Chile in red. A gold measuring bar draws from the northern tip to Cape Horn; the number counts to 4,270 km.

beats.text: It starts in one of the driest deserts on Earth, and ends among *glaciers.*
beats.visual: Fly to the north: the desert turns sand-gold, pin ATACAMA DESERT; then fly all the way south: the two ice fields along the border turn white-blue, pin GLACIERS.

beats.text: Slide it over Europe, and it reaches from the top of Norway past the bottom of *Spain.*
beats.visual: Map of Europe. A red copy of Chile slides up from below and stops with its top on Norway's Arctic tip (teal line TOP OF NORWAY); a gold line BOTTOM OF SPAIN; its tail runs past it (white dot).

beats.text: But side to side, it averages just *177* kilometers.
beats.visual: Back on the whole country with the tall 4,270 ruler: a short teal bar measures across the middle; on '177' a round magnifier grows out of it and shows the narrow strip up close, the counter under it counts to 177 KM.
A big gold question mark pops beside the sliver.
The ocean west of Chile brightens blue with moving wave lines; label PACIFIC OCEAN.

beats.text: On the other, the Andes, the longest mountain range on any *continent.*
beats.visual: A chain of mountain peaks rises one by one down the eastern edge; label ANDES.

beats.text: You see, in 1881, Chile and Argentina signed a border *treaty.*
beats.visual: Whole country above the captions. Year 1881 stamps in above Chile's tip; CHILE red, ARGENTINA blue are named; then the names give way to a treaty paper with two signatures.

beats.text: The line would follow the highest *peaks* of the Andes.
beats.visual: A bright white border line draws itself south along the mountain chain, every peak lighting up as the pen point passes it.

beats.text: So Chile kept the narrow strip between the mountains and the *sea.*
beats.visual: Pull back: the strip between the white line and the coast fills red, north to south.

beats.text: It's not a strange shape. It's the edge of a *continent.*
beats.visual: Pull back until all of South America fills the frame (Panama at the top edge); Chile is simply its glowing western edge; '24X' returns small on the South Atlantic.
